Chapter 1 — Signal on the Dark Line
The first tunnel was crowded with echoforms that imitated human memories.
They spoke in human voices, but none could answer a question.
I recovered an intact record fragment after the battle. It should open the next section.
The fragment preserved an evacuation order from the old station.
Someone had deliberately erased the destination of the final train.
I found new coordinates beneath the erased layer. They lead inside the sealed sector.
The coordinates led to a sealed bell-tower relay.
There is a rhythm like a living pulse inside the signal. It may be a survivor.
But an echoform cluster has already surrounded the relay. We need to hurry.
The Lamplighters are a small restoration crew that keeps moving even through afterglow storms.
I heard a rescue call from a line that is not on the map. The signal is still alive.
We verify it and restore the route. Everyone, prepare to depart.
The sealed platform kept calling the names of passengers who no longer existed.
What matters is not whether a rescue signal is real, but who is hearing it now.
Erase our names from the old list and leave our current coordinates behind.
Power flowed backward, and platforms we had already crossed lit their incomplete signs again.
The line is not malicious. It is only an automated procedure running long after it should have stopped.
If we stop the central gate, at least this section's false calls can end.
The underground return chamber was lined like a wall with formation charts containing only vacant seats.
This core is not looking for people. It is trying to fill empty slots.
We will stop not the past, but the command that erases the present.
The three unique boss records retained the same short handshake pattern.
Signals are lighting one by one from the terminus back toward the origin, not in the direction of travel.
It is not time travel. A damaged return procedure is fitting us into a past record.
When the return formation core stopped, the inverted signal lights turned back toward their proper direction.
Not every record vanished, but none could place a present person into a past empty seat again.
One true beacon remains, facing outward. We choose how to connect the next route.
The central junction panels classified the expedition as an enemy formation from long ago.
We do not need to smash the panels. We need a gap to terminate the return directive.
When the gate opens, we cross at once. No one is staying behind in a returning record.
When the Hollow Engine stopped, the erased destination returned.
The final train had not been bound for a lost city, but for a refuge still in motion.
The first line is connected again. Let us head for the next light.
The massive Hollow Engine awoke, swallowing the light along the rails.
Check your lights and equipment. From here on, one mistake is too many.
We are not protecting the rails. We are protecting the stories of the people waiting at their end.
After the Great Blackout, the mineral railway beneath the earth became the last route connecting the surviving cities.
A newly awakened record navigator must restore broken lights and the memories carried between them.
The first signal is blinking at Platform Seven. We start there.
I will clear the reconnaissance route. Follow as soon as the signal comes alive.
I gathered broken station announcements and turned them into a little chorus.
A trace that someone lived matters more to me than perfect pitch.
Let us play it together at the next station. It will sound better than listening alone.
Before departure, I even check the seatbelt on the empty seat. I cannot relax if I skip it.
I began doing it so I would not forget the teammate who never returned.
Today I placed new rescue gear there. An empty place can help save the next person now.
